items.informal_name: Vanishing of derivatives at a multiple root
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {A : Type u_3} [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] (p : Polynomial R)
  (q : ℕ) (r : A) {p' : Polynomial A},
  Polynomial.map (algebraMap R A) p = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C r) ^ q * p' →
    ∀ {k : ℕ}, k < q → (Polynomial.aeval r) ((⇑Polynomial.derivative)^[k] p) = 0
items.informal_description: Let `R` and `A` be commutative rings, where `A` is an `R`-algebra. Let `p` be a polynomial in `R[X]`, `r` an element in `A`, and `q` a natural number. Let `\bar{p}` be the image of `p` in `A[X]` under the canonical map. If `(X - r)^q` divides `\bar{p}`, then for any natural number `k < q`, the `k`-th derivative of `p` evaluated at `r` is zero, i.e., `p^{(k)}(r) = 0`.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of the Sum of Iterated Derivatives of a Polynomial at a Multiple Root
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (A : Type u_3) [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] [Nontrivial A]
  [NoZeroDivisors A] (p : Polynomial R) {q : ℕ},
  0 < q →
    Function.Injective ⇑(algebraMap R A) →
      ∃ gp,
        gp.natDegree ≤ p.natDegree - q ∧
          ∀ (r : A) {p' : Polynomial A},
            Polynomial.map (algebraMap R A) p = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C r) ^ (q - 1) * p' →
              (Polynomial.aeval r) (Polynomial.sumIDeriv p) =
                (q - 1).fa...
items.informal_description:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ be a nontrivial $R$-algebra that is a ring with no zero divisors. Assume the canonical map from $R$ to $A$ is injective. For any polynomial $p(X) \in R[X]$ and any positive integer $q$, there exists a polynomial $g_p(X) \in R[X]$ with degree at most $\deg(p) - q$ satisfying the following property: for any $r \in A$ and any polynomial $p'(X) \in A[X]$, if the image of $p(X)$ in $A[X]$ can be written as $p(X) = (X-r)^{q-1} p'(X)$, then
$$ \left(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} p^{(i)}\right)(r) = (q-1)! \cdot p'(r) + q! \cdot g_p(r), $$
where $p^{(i)}$ denotes the $i$-th formal derivative of $p$, and all evaluations are performed in $A$. The sum is finite as derivatives of order higher than the degree of the polynomial are zero.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative Zero for Order Greater than Degree
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ), p.natDegree < n → (Polynomial.hasseDeriv n) p = 0
items.informal_description: If the natural degree of a polynomial $ p $ is less than $ n $, then the $ n $-th Hasse derivative of $ p $ is the zero polynomial, i.e., $ \text{hasseDeriv}^n(p) = 0 $.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Sum of Iterated Derivatives with Factorial Multiplicity
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (A : Type u_3) [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] (p : Polynomial R)
  (q : ℕ),
  ∃ gp,
    gp.natDegree ≤ p.natDegree - q ∧
      ∀ (r : A),
        (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C r) ^ q ∣ Polynomial.map (algebraMap R A) p →
          (Polynomial.aeval r) (Polynomial.sumIDeriv p) = q.factorial • (Polynomial.aeval r) gp
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a ring $ R $ and natural number $ q $, there exists a polynomial $ g_p $ with $ \deg(g_p) \leq \deg(p) - q $ such that for every element $ r $ in an $ R $-algebra $ A $, if $ (X - r)^q $ divides $ p $ under the canonical algebra map $ R \to A $, then the evaluation of the sum of all iterated derivatives of $ p $ at $ r $ equals $ q! \cdot \text{eval}_r(g_p) $.

items.informal_name: Roots of Polynomial Dividing Derivative Product Imply Roots of Another Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] [NoZeroDivisors R] [CharZero R] {f g : Polynomial R},
  f ≠ 0 → f ∣ Polynomial.derivative f * g → ∀ {a : R}, f.IsRoot a → g.IsRoot a
items.informal_description: In a ring of characteristic zero, if a non-zero polynomial $ f $ divides the product of its derivative $ f' $ and another polynomial $ g $, then every root $ a $ of $ f $ is also a root of $ g $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.
